pages.body:
# Send a design to your machine

Before you send, set up your machine in [Lilo Link](lilo-link-wifi.md).

## Steps

1. Press **Send** at the top right of the editor. It is greyed out until the design has stitches.
2. The **Send to machine** window opens. It says how many stitches and colour changes the file has.
3. Read **Before you sew**. It lists the needle, stabiliser and hooping tips for your fabric.
4. Check the **Machine** list. Pick your machine. Press **Search network** if it is missing.
5. Press **Send**.
6. A progress line shows how many bytes have gone across. When it finishes it says **Sent** and the name the machine stored it under.

Lilo sends a **PES** file, the format Brother and Baby Lock use. The file keeps your thread colours.

## What the warnings at the top mean

The window can list warnings about the design, like stitches that were too long and were split. Read them before you send. Read [What the warnings mean](warnings-explained.md).

## On the machine

The design appears in the machine's memory or its Wi-Fi inbox. The exact place depends on the model, so follow the machine's own manual to open it.

## If a file with the same name exists

Lilo asks you to confirm before it replaces it. Rename the project in the top bar if you want to keep both.

## If it fails

Lilo shows a plain message. Look it up in [Wi-Fi troubleshooting](send-troubleshooting.md).

## Sending from Lilo Link

You can also send from **Lilo Link**, **Machines**, with the **Send** button next to a saved machine. That page also sends an existing file.

## Sending to another make of machine

Use **Export** and save a file for the machine. Read [Choosing a format](export-formats.md) and [USB stick](usb-stick.md).

pages.title: Use a USB stick instead
pages.summary: Save a file, copy it to the root of a USB stick and load it on any machine. Keep it to 12 designs or fewer.

headings.text: If the machine does not show the file

pages.body:
# Use a USB stick instead

A USB stick always works. Use it when:

- your machine has no Wi-Fi,
- the Wi-Fi is not stable, or
- you are sewing at a place with no network.

## Steps

1. Press **Export**.
2. Choose the **file format** your machine reads. For Brother and Baby Lock, choose **PES**. Read [Choosing a format](export-formats.md).
3. Press **Save**. Pick the USB stick as the place to save.
4. Eject the stick safely. On Mac, drag it to the bin. On Windows, use **Safely Remove Hardware**.
5. Put the stick in the machine and open it from the machine's screen.

## Rules for the stick

- **Put the files at the root.** That means the first screen of the stick, not inside a folder. Many machines do not look in folders.
- **Keep to 12 designs or fewer.** Many home machines show only the first 12 files. If you have more, make a second stick.
- **Use a small stick** formatted FAT32. A very large stick can fail to read.
- **Use plain file names:** letters and numbers, no accents or symbols.

## If the machine does not show the file

- Check the format. The machine only lists formats it can read.
- Check that the file is not in a folder.
- Count the files. Is it more than 12?
- Try another stick.

## Related

[Set up Wi-Fi sending with Lilo Link](lilo-link-wifi.md), [File formats](formats-reference.md)

pages.title: Wi-Fi troubleshooting
pages.summary: Every message Lilo Link can show when a send fails, what it means and what to do.
pages.body:
# Wi-Fi troubleshooting

When a send fails, Lilo shows a short message. Under the message is a **code**, a short word with an underscore. Find your code below.

First check the basics:

1. The machine is **on** and awake.
2. It is on a **2.4 GHz** network, the **same network** as your computer. Read [Set up Wi-Fi sending](lilo-link-wifi.md).
3. Nothing else is sending to it.

## Codes

### `machine_unreachable`
"Machine unreachable." Lilo cannot connect at all. The machine is off, asleep, on a different network or has a new address. **Do this:** turn the machine on, check its Wi-Fi, press **Scan network** again.

### `machine_timeout`
"Request to machine timed out." The machine did not answer in time. **Do this:** wake the machine, move closer to the router and try again.

### `device_busy`
"The machine is busy with another transfer." Another send is in progress. **Do this:** wait a minute, or restart the machine.

### `delivery_unknown`
"Delivery could not be confirmed. Check the file on the device before sending again." The file may have arrived, but the machine did not confirm. **Do this:** look in the machine's file list before you send again. Sending twice could make a copy.

### `identity_changed`
"The device identity changed. Scan again and select the intended machine." The address now belongs to a different device. **Do this:** scan again and save the right machine.

### `unsupported_operation`
"This device does not support that operation." The machine cannot do what Lilo asked, like listing storage. **Do this:** use another way, such as a [USB stick](usb-stick.md).

### `file_exists`
"A file with this name exists. Confirm replacement before sending." **Do this:** rename the project, or confirm the replacement.

### `protocol_error`
"Protocol error." The machine answered in a way Lilo did not expect. **Do this:** update Lilo and the machine's software, then try again. If it keeps happening, [report a bug](bug-reports.md).

### `machine_rejected`
"Machine rejected the request (machine error code N)." The machine understood and said no. **Do this:** read the number on the machine's screen. Check its manual. Often the file is too complex or the machine is in a mode that does not accept designs.

### `file_too_large`
"Design is N bytes but the machine accepts at most N bytes." **Do this:** make the design smaller or use fewer stitches. Choose **Standard** quality. Read [Standard or Premium](standard-vs-premium.md).

### `insufficient_storage`
"Not enough free memory on the machine." **Do this:** delete old designs from the machine's memory.

### `unsupported_format`
"Unsupported design format; this machine accepts ..." **Do this:** export a format the machine accepts. Read [File formats](formats-reference.md).

### `upload_failed`
"Upload rejected with HTTP status N." The upload was refused part-way. **Do this:** try again. If it repeats, restart the machine and Lilo.

### `pairing_required`
"Machine requires pairing." The machine wants to approve this computer first. A hint says what to press on the machine. **Do this:** follow the hint on the machine's screen, then send again.

### `invalid_ip`
"Is not an IP address." The address you typed is wrong. **Do this:** type four numbers separated by dots, like 192.168.1.50.

### `missing_ip`
An address is needed to test or send. **Do this:** choose a machine first.

### `missing_filename`
A file name is required. **Do this:** give your project a name in the top bar.

### `cancelled`
"Transfer cancelled." You (or something else) stopped the send. Send again if you want it.

### `updating`
"Bridge is updating." Lilo is installing an update. **Do this:** wait until it restarts.

### `unauthorized`
"Missing or invalid API token." The window and Lilo's built-in connection service lost touch. **Do this:** restart Lilo.

### `not_found`
The thing Lilo asked about (a saved machine or a transfer) does not exist any more. **Do this:** refresh the Machines list.

### `internal_error`
Something went wrong inside Lilo. **Do this:** open **Lilo Link**, then **Logs**, and [report a bug](bug-reports.md) with the log text.

## Less common codes

These come from Lilo's built-in connection service. You will rarely see them. Most need only a retry or a restart.

### `ip_not_local`
Lilo refuses to contact an address that is not on your home or office network. **Do this:** use the address shown on the machine's own network screen. It usually starts with 192.168 or 10.

### `discovery_running`
A network scan is already running. **Do this:** wait for it to finish.

### `queue_full`
The send queue is full. **Do this:** wait for the current sends to finish, then try again.

### `previous_delivery_unknown`
An earlier send to this machine was never confirmed. **Do this:** check the machine's file list, resolve that send first, then send again.

### `not_cancellable`
Only a send that is queued or waiting can be cancelled. **Do this:** wait for it to end.

### `not_uncertain`
This send does not need a confirmation. **Do this:** nothing. Refresh the Logs page.

### `empty_body`
The file to send was empty. **Do this:** export the design again and check it has stitches.

### `invalid_filename`
The file name has a folder or odd characters in it. **Do this:** rename the project with letters and numbers only.

### `confirmation_required`
Deleting a file from a machine needs your confirmation. **Do this:** confirm in Lilo Link.

### `identity_required`
Lilo must read the machine's status before it deletes a file. **Do this:** press **Test** on the machine first.

### `pairing_in_progress`
Another pairing request is waiting for a decision. **Do this:** wait a moment and try again.

### `pairing_origin_mismatch`
A pairing request belongs to a different source. **Do this:** start the pairing again from Lilo.

### `origin_required`
Pairing only works from a web page. **Do this:** read the token in Lilo Link, **Settings**.

### `origin_not_allowed`
The web page asking to connect is not on the allowed list. **Do this:** only allow sites you trust.

### `invalid_origin`
A web address was not in the right shape. **Do this:** use a full address, like https://example.com.

## Still stuck?

[Use a USB stick](usb-stick.md) while you sort it out. Your design is safe.

pages.title: Choosing a format and exporting
pages.summary: Pick the right file format for your machine, set a name and origin, and save.
pages.body:
# Choosing a format and exporting

Press **Export** at the top right. It is greyed out until the design has stitches.

## Choose the format

Under **File format**, press the one your machine reads. If you do not know:

- **Brother or Baby Lock:** PES.
- **Janome:** JEF.
- **Pfaff or Husqvarna Viking:** VP3.
- **Singer:** XXX.
- **Commercial multi-needle machines:** DST.
- **Melco:** EXP. **Barudan:** U01. **Tajima with colours:** TBF.
- **Older Husqvarna Viking:** HUS. **Pfaff and Viking with exact colours:** VIP.
- **CNC, plotter and DIY tools:** G-code, a stitch path that Lilo writes but cannot read back.

There is also a **PNG** picture of the design. Use it for emails and mock-ups.

Read [File formats](formats-reference.md) for the full list. Formats such as DST, EXP and U01 do not keep thread colours.

## The details

The window shows **Export stats**: stitches, colour changes, size and time. Check them.

- **File name:** set the name. Lilo adds the right ending.
- **Origin point:** where the design's zero sits in the hoop. The centre is right for most machines. Some commercial machines start from a corner.

## Before you sew

The **Before you sew** list sits in the same window. It lists the needle, stabiliser and hooping tips for your fabric. Read it, then press **Save**.

## Warnings

Warnings list anything that may sew badly, like stitches longer than 12 mm that Lilo had to split. Read [What the warnings mean](warnings-explained.md).

## Press Save

Press **Save**. Your computer asks where to put the file. Choose a USB stick for a machine without Wi-Fi. Read [USB stick](usb-stick.md).

Saving ticks the **Send** step in the workflow strip.

pages.title: Pixel art
pages.summary: Paint a grid of squares and stitch each one as a block, a cross or a satin bar. Good for small badges and patterns.
pages.body:
# Pixel art

**Pixel art** is a picture made of square cells, like a tiny mosaic or a cross-stitch chart. Open it from **Home** or the **Pixel art** view.

## The tools

- **Pencil (B)** paints cells. Drag to paint many.
- **Fill (G)** fills a connected area of one colour.
- **Erase (E)** clears cells. A cleared cell has no stitches.
- **Eyedropper (I)** picks the colour of a cell.
- **Line (L)** drags a straight line.
- **Rectangle (R)** drags a rectangle. **Filled rectangles** switches between outline and solid.

**Undo**, **Redo** and **Clear** sit under the tools.

## Colours

Pick a **Palette brand** and **Palette line**. Click a swatch to paint with that thread. **Colours in the picture** lists what you have used.

## The grid

Set the **Grid width** and **Grid height** in cells, then press **Resize**. Set the **Cell size in millimetres**. A 32 by 32 grid with 2 mm cells makes a 64 mm design.

## Stitch style

- **Tatami:** each cell is a block of fill rows. Solid and flat.
- **Cross:** an X in each cell. Looks like cross-stitch.
- **Satin:** a satin bar across each cell. Shiny.

## From a picture

Press **Import a picture…** to turn a picture into pixels. Set **Most colours** and decide whether to **Keep the background**. Then tidy it with the pencil.

## Preview and send

The **Stitch preview** on the right plays your pixel art. Press **Send to editor** to add the stitches to the editor's design, where you can resize, combine and send it. Or press **Export…** to save a file.

## Tips

- Use big cells (2 to 3 mm) for a clean sew.
- Use few colours. Each one is a thread change. Read [Fewer colour changes](fewer-colour-changes.md).
- Test sew first. Tiny cells can pile up thread.

pages.title: The converter
pages.summary: Change an embroidery file to another format, or turn pictures into stitches or a traced SVG, many files at once.
pages.body:
# The converter

The **converter** changes files from one format to another. Use it when a client sends a DST and your machine needs a PES.

## Steps

1. Open **Converter** from the top of the window.
2. Drop files onto the box, or press **Choose files…**. You can use embroidery files (PES, DST, JEF, VP3, EXP, XXX, U01, PEC, HUS, VIP, TBF) or pictures (PNG, JPG, WEBP, SVG).
3. Tick the formats you want. You can tick several.
4. Press **Convert**.
5. Under **Results**, press **Save…** next to a result, or **Save all**.

You can remove a file from the list with its **Remove** button, or clear the whole list.

## Open in the editor

Press **Open in editor** on an embroidery file to add its stitches to the editor as **Manual stitch** shapes. You can then move and resize them. You cannot change their stitch type, because the original instructions are fixed stitch points.

## Warnings

Conversions can lose something. The results list shows a warning when:

- the source file had no thread colours,
- the target format cannot keep colours,
- stops were converted,
- stitches were longer than the target allows.

Read the warnings before you save. Formats such as DST, EXP and U01 do not keep thread colours. Read [File formats](formats-reference.md).

## Pictures

A picture can become **stitches** (with the same auto-digitize as the editor) or a **traced SVG** you can edit in a drawing app.

## Related

[Opening files](opening-files.md)

headings.text: When a file will not open

pages.body:
# Opening files

Lilo opens three kinds of files.

## Pictures: PNG, JPG, WEBP, SVG

Open a picture to digitize it. Use **Digitize a picture…** on Home, **Open image…** in the left panel, or drop the file on the canvas. Read [Turn a picture into stitches](auto-digitize.md).

SVG files are drawings. They trace more cleanly than photos.

## Lilo projects: .lilo

A **.lilo** file is a full project: shapes, settings, reference images and version history. Open with **Open…** on Home or **⌘O**. Double-clicking a .lilo file opens it in Lilo. Read [Projects and autosave](projects-and-autosave.md).

## Embroidery files

Lilo reads PES, DST, JEF, VP3, EXP, XXX, U01, PEC, HUS, VIP and TBF, and writes those plus G-code (a stitch path for CNC and plotter tools, write only). Use the [converter](converter.md) to change a file's format, or press **Open in editor** there to bring the stitches into the editor.

A file that has already been stitched has fixed needle points. Lilo shows them as **Manual stitch** shapes. You can move, resize and re-colour them, but you cannot change a fill's pattern, because the pattern is gone.

## When a file will not open

- Check the ending. Lilo does not read every format. See [File formats](formats-reference.md).
- Very large files may be slow. Close other windows.
- If a file is damaged, try the original from where you got it.

## Where projects live

New projects save to **Documents, then Lilo**. Home shows the most recent ones as cards with a thumbnail.

pages.title: Projects and autosave
pages.summary: How .lilo project files work, where they are saved and how autosave protects your work.
pages.body:
# Projects and autosave

A **project** is your whole design in one file with the ending **.lilo**. It holds your shapes, settings, reference pictures and a small preview image.

## The File menu

The **File** menu in the top-left of the editor has:

- **New design** (**⌘N**)
- **Open project…** (**⌘O**)
- **Save** (**⌘S**)
- **Save As…** (**⇧⌘S**)
- **Revert to saved**, which throws away changes since your last save
- **Version history**
- Open image, Export and Send

## Where files go

The first time you save, Lilo suggests **Documents, then Lilo**. You can save anywhere. Home lists recent projects, newest first, with a thumbnail.

A small dot next to the project name means you have unsaved changes.

## Autosave

Lilo saves a copy of your work every **30 seconds** and when you click away from the window. These copies go into the project's own **version history**, not over your last real save. So autosave never destroys a save you chose to keep.

If Lilo closes by accident, open the project again and look in **Version history**.

## Opening a project

Use **Open…** on Home, **⌘O**, or double-click a .lilo file. Lilo asks before it throws away unsaved changes in the current design.

## Name your project

Click the name in the top bar and type. A good name is the job: "JK lining monogram". It also becomes the default file name when you export.

## Related

[Version history](version-history.md)

pages.title: Version history
pages.summary: Browse the last 50 saved versions of a project, preview one and bring it back.
pages.body:
# Version history

Every project keeps its **last 50 versions**. Each save and each autosave adds one. When there are more than 50, the oldest drops off.

## Open it

Open the **File** menu and choose **Version history**.

## What you see

- A list of saved versions, newest first, each with its time.
- A **Preview** of the selected version.

## Bring one back

1. Click a version to see its preview.
2. Press **Restore this version**, or double-click the version.

Restoring replaces your current work with that version. If you are not sure, save a copy first with **Save As…**.

## Undo is different

**Undo** (⌘Z) steps back through your edits in the current session, up to 200 steps. **Version history** is for bigger jumps, or for when you closed the app.

## Related

[Projects and autosave](projects-and-autosave.md)

pages.summary: The 12 embroidery file formats Lilo writes (all but G-code it also reads), and which machines use each one.
pages.body:
# File formats

Lilo writes 12 embroidery formats and reads 11 of them. The list is built from the app's own format table.

A format is the file type your machine understands. Brother and Baby Lock machines use **PES**. Most commercial machines use **DST**. If you are not sure, check your machine manual or the type of file it already sews.

| Extension | Name | Lilo | Keeps thread colours? | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| .pes | Brother PES | Read and write | Yes | Brother, Baby Lock, Bernina (reads) |
| .pec | Brother PEC | Read and write | Yes | Brother, Baby Lock |
| .dst | Tajima DST | Read and write | No | Tajima, Barudan, Ricoma, Melco, SWF, Happy, ZSK, Toyota, Janome MB-7, Brother, Baby Lock |
| .exp | Melco EXP | Read and write | No | Melco, Bernina |
| .jef | Janome JEF | Read and write | Yes | Janome, Elna (some) |
| .vp3 | Pfaff/Viking VP3 | Read and write | Yes | Pfaff, Husqvarna Viking |
| .xxx | Singer XXX | Read and write | Yes | Singer, Compucon |
| .u01 | Barudan U01 | Read and write | No | Barudan |
| .hus | Husqvarna Viking HUS | Read and write | Yes | Husqvarna Viking |
| .vip | Pfaff/Viking VIP | Read and write | Yes | Husqvarna Viking, Pfaff |
| .tbf | Tajima TBF | Read and write | Yes | Tajima |
| .gcode | G-code (stitch path) | Write only | No | CNC and plotter tools |

**Keeps thread colours** matters when you send a file. Formats without colours still sew in the right order. They just show you "colour 1, colour 2" instead of real thread names. See [Choosing a format](export-formats.md).

## Machine compatibility

The research behind Lilo covers 17 brands, 66 machines and 44 thread brands. No machine has been tested on real hardware beyond one pending Brother run, so treat every machine as "should work" until you have sewn one design. The full tables are in compatibility.md in the docs folder.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.summary: Plain-word meanings for every embroidery and Lilo term, from appliqué to zig-zag.
pages.body:
# Glossary

Words are in alphabetical order. A word in **bold** inside a meaning has its own entry.

## A to C

- **Appliqué.** A patch of cloth stitched onto a garment. An **E-stitch** edge is often used to hold it.
- **Aspect ratio.** The relationship between width and height. Locking it keeps a shape from squashing.
- **Auto digitize.** Lilo turns a picture into stitches in one step. Read [Turn a picture into stitches](auto-digitize.md).
- **Backing.** Another word for **stabiliser**.
- **Bean stitch.** Another name for a **triple** run.
- **Birdnesting.** A tangle of thread under the cloth that jams the machine.
- **Bobbin.** The small spool under the needle plate that makes the back of the stitch.
- **Colour block.** A run of shapes sewn in one thread, with no thread change inside.
- **Colour change.** A stop to swap the top thread for the next colour.
- **Column.** A **satin** stripe. Its width is the distance across it.
- **Cut-away.** A **stabiliser** you trim around the design. It stays in the garment.

## D to H

- **Density.** How close stitches sit together. A smaller gap means higher density.
- **Digitizing.** Turning a picture or drawing into stitch instructions.
- **DST.** A file format used by many commercial machines. It does not keep thread colours.
- **E-stitch.** A comb-shaped run stitch.
- **Edge outline.** A running line sewn round the edge of a **fill**.
- **Fill.** Rows of stitches covering an area.
- **Font (embroidery).** Letters drawn to be sewn, with a height range where they sew well.
- **Format.** The kind of file a machine reads, like PES or DST.
- **Gradient.** A fade in a **fill**, made by changing row spacing across the shape.
- **Hoop.** The frame that holds cloth tight while it is sewn.

## I to O

- **Inset.** How far inside the edge an **underlay** stops, so it stays hidden.
- **Jump.** Thread that travels from one point to another without sewing.
- **Knit.** Stretchy cloth. It needs more **pull compensation** and a firm **stabiliser**.
- **Lilo Link.** The part of Lilo that sends designs to a machine over Wi-Fi.
- **Lock stitches.** Tiny stitches at the start and end of a run that stop it unravelling. Also called tie-in and tie-off.
- **Manual stitch.** A stitch placed exactly where you click.
- **Monogram.** Initials sewn as a mark, like "JK" inside a jacket.
- **Motif.** A small shape repeated across a **fill**.
- **Needle drop.** One point where the needle goes through the cloth. Also called a stitch.
- **Needle size.** The thickness of the needle, like 75/11.
- **Origin.** The point in the design that sits at the centre of the hoop.

## P to S

- **PES.** The file format of Brother and Baby Lock machines. It keeps thread colours.
- **Pile.** The fluffy surface of cloth like towel or velvet.
- **Pull compensation.** Making a shape slightly bigger to allow for the thread pulling cloth inward.
- **Pucker.** Ripples in the cloth around a design.
- **Realistic view.** A preview that draws each stitch as shaded thread.
- **Registration.** How well one shape lines up with its neighbour.
- **Row spacing.** The gap between rows of stitches in a **fill**.
- **Run.** A stitch that follows a line.
- **Satin.** Side-to-side stitches in a column. Smooth and shiny.
- **Sew-out.** The real stitched result.
- **Sewing area.** The part of the hoop the machine can sew.
- **Stabiliser.** A sheet under the cloth that stops it moving and bunching.
- **Stitch length.** The distance between two needle drops.
- **Split satin.** A wide **satin** column divided so no stitch is too long.

## T to Z

- **Tatami.** The common name for a standard **fill** with offset rows.
- **Tear-away.** A **stabiliser** that rips off after sewing.
- **Thread weight.** How thin thread is. 40 wt is standard. 60 wt is finer.
- **Tie-in and tie-off.** See **lock stitches**.
- **Tolerance.** How far a stitch may stray from the line you drew.
- **Topping.** A thin water-soluble sheet on top of fluffy cloth.
- **Trim.** A cut of the thread between shapes, done by the machine.
- **Underlay.** Light stitches sewn first, under the top stitches.
- **Underpath.** Travelling through a **fill** under the stitches instead of jumping.
- **Zig-zag underlay.** An **underlay** that goes back and forth across a column.

pages.title: Fixing sew-out problems
pages.summary: Puckering, gaps, thread breaks and birdnesting: what causes each and which Lilo setting to change.

headings.text: Outline does not line up with the fill

pages.body:
# Fixing sew-out problems

A **sew-out** is the real stitched result. When it looks wrong, find your symptom below. Each one lists the cause and the Lilo setting that helps. Change one thing at a time and sew a small test again.

## Puckering

The cloth bunches up or ripples around the design.

**Causes and fixes:**

1. **Too dense.** Too many stitches in a small area. Raise **Row spacing** (fill) or **Density** (satin). Check for a density warning.
2. **Not enough underlay.** Turn on **Underlay**. Read [Underlay and pull compensation](underlay-and-pull.md).
3. **Wrong stabiliser.** Use cut-away for knits and thin cloth. See [Sewing setup presets](sewing-presets.md).
4. **Hooped too tight or stretched.** The cloth springs back. Hoop firm, not stretched.
5. **Wrong fabric in the Sewing setup.** Pick the one that matches.

## Gaps

White cloth shows between a fill and its outline, or between two shapes.

**Causes and fixes:**

1. **Pull compensation too low.** The thread pulled the shapes in. Raise **Pull compensation**.
2. **Cloth moved.** Use firmer stabiliser and hoop tighter.
3. **Shapes did not overlap.** Slightly enlarge one of them, or let Lilo overlap columns with **Premium** quality.
4. **Fill underlay missing.** The fill sank into the cloth. Turn on underlay.

![A fill with a gap to its outline, and the fixed version](screenshots/gap-fix.png)

## Thread breaks

The top thread snaps again and again.

**Causes and fixes:**

1. **Stitches too dense.** Needle holes cut the thread. Raise spacing. A density warning is a clue.
2. **Tiny stitches piled up.** Use **Standard** quality, or raise stitch length. Tiny stitches are merged automatically.
3. **Old or wrong needle.** Replace it. Use the size in **Before you sew**.
4. **Thread too thick for the detail.** Use **60 wt** for tiny letters.
5. **Poor or dry thread.** Try a fresh spool.

## Birdnesting

A tangled lump of thread forms under the cloth, and the machine jams.

**Causes and fixes:**

1. **The top thread slipped out of tension.** Rethread the top thread with the presser foot **up**.
2. **Fluff in the bobbin area.** Clean the bobbin case.
3. **Hoop not seated.** Cloth lifting off the plate. Re-hoop.
4. **Long jump at the start.** In Lilo, move the start point close to where sewing begins. Use **Start** in the shape bar.

Lilo cannot see your machine. The first two causes are in the machine.

## Bobbin thread shows on top

The top thread is too tight. Loosen the top tension a little. Read your machine's manual.

## Outline does not line up with the fill

Called **registration**. Cloth shifted. Use firm stabiliser, tighter hoop and **Pull compensation** on the fill.

## Letters look filled in

Letters are too small for the thread. Read [Small letters](small-letters.md).

## Always sew a test

Before the real garment, sew the design on a scrap of the same cloth with the same stabiliser. It takes minutes and saves a ruined jacket.

pages.title: What the warnings mean
pages.summary: Every warning Lilo can show in the tray and in Export or Send, what it means and how to fix it.

headings.text: A high stitch count or long sewing time

pages.body:
# What the warnings mean

Lilo watches your design while you work. When something might sew badly, a short note appears in the **warnings tray**, in the right-hand column, under the Sewing setup card. It never blocks you. Each note offers a **fix** button or a **Read more** link. You can dismiss any note.

## Outside the hoop

The design is bigger than the hoop's sewing area. The machine cannot sew what is outside.

**Fix:** pick a larger hoop (**Smallest hoop that fits**), or scale the design down. Read [Sizing and hoops](sizing-and-hoops.md).

## Too dense

Too many stitches land in the same 1 square millimetre. The thread may break or the cloth may pucker.

**Fix:** open the shape's settings and raise **Row spacing** (fills) or **Density** (satin). Read [Fixing sew-out problems](sewout-troubleshooting.md).

## A stitch was too long

Stitches over 12 mm can snag, so Lilo split them. The design is fine, but long stitches often mean a big, open fill.

**Fix:** shorten **Stitch length** in a fill, or use a pattern with shorter stitches.

## Satin too thin

A satin column is narrower than the thread can cover well: under 1.5 mm with 40 wt thread, or under 1 mm with 60 wt. It will not look shiny. Stitches pile up and the thread can break.

**Fix:** turn it into a running stitch, make it wider, or switch to **60 wt**. Lilo still makes the file. See [Stitch safety](stitch-safety.md).

## A long stitch can snag

Some stitches are longer than 7 mm and the fabric is something you wear. Long stitches can catch on fingers and buttons. Lilo only splits stitches over 12 mm.

**Fix:** shorten **Stitch length** in a fill or run. Read [Stitch safety](stitch-safety.md).

## A shape made no stitches

A shape could not be stitched, for example if its thread is missing. **Fix:** select the shape and give it a thread.

## The design is empty

Nothing to sew yet. Draw, type or open a picture.

## Many colour changes

More than 8 colour changes. Each is a stop to swap thread on a home machine.

**Fix:** merge similar colours. Read [Fewer colour changes](fewer-colour-changes.md).

## A high stitch count or long sewing time

A design with more than about 30,000 stitches, or over an hour of sewing at 850 stitches a minute (counting stops for thread changes and cuts), is a long sew and a bigger file.

**Fix:** make it smaller, use **Standard** quality, or use fewer fills.

## Tiny regions

A shape under about 1 mm wide is too small to sew as a fill. It will blur or snap thread.

**Fix:** delete it, make it bigger, or turn it into a **Triple** run.

## Satin too wide

A satin column over 8 mm with no split has long, loose stitches.

**Fix:** turn on **Split above** in the **Satin** section, or change the shape to a fill. Read [Satin tips](satin-tips.md).

## Letters too small

The letters are shorter than 6 mm with 40 wt thread, or 4 mm with 60 wt. They will fill in.

**Fix:** make them taller or switch to **60 wt**. Read [Small letters](small-letters.md).

## Fonts and text

- **Below or above the font's range:** the font suits another height. Pick a different font.
- **Custom font small:** custom fonts sew best above a minimum height.
- **Missing glyph:** the font has no letter for a character you typed.
- **Text longer than the path:** the end would run off the curve.

## About dismissing

A dismissed note stays hidden until the problem changes. Reopening the project shows it again.

# Frequently asked questions

## Does Lilo cost anything?

No. Lilo is free and open source under the GPL-3.0 licence.

## Do I need an account?

No. There is no sign-in.

## Where do my designs go?

They stay on your computer. Lilo only contacts one place: the GitHub Releases page, to check for updates once a day. You can switch that off.

## Which machines can I send to over Wi-Fi?

Brother and Baby Lock machines with built-in Wi-Fi. Every other machine works through a file on a USB stick. Read [Set up Wi-Fi sending](lilo-link-wifi.md) and [USB stick](usb-stick.md).

## My machine is on a 5 GHz network. Will it work?

Most embroidery machines only use 2.4 GHz. Connect the machine to 2.4 GHz. Your computer can be on either band if both bands share one network.

## Can I stitch a photo?

You can, but photos turn out muddy. Thread has no soft shading. Use a simple logo or drawing, or reduce the photo to a few flat colours first.

## What is the biggest design I can make?

It depends on your hoop. The sewing area of the hoop is the limit. Read [Sizing and hoops](sizing-and-hoops.md).

## Why does my design look smaller when sewn?

Thread pulls the cloth in. Raise **Pull compensation**. Read [Underlay and pull compensation](underlay-and-pull.md).

## Why are my letters filled in?

They are too small for the thread. Read [Small letters](small-letters.md).

## Can I use my own fonts?

Yes. TTF, OTF and TTC files. Read [Using your own fonts](own-fonts.md).

## Can I turn off the tour and the tips?

You can skip the tour at any step. Hints only show when you ask for them. Dismiss a warning note with its close button.

## How do I replay the tour?

Open **Help** and press **Replay the tour**.

## What if Lilo closes without saving?

Lilo autosaves every 30 seconds. Reopen the project and look in **Version history**. Read [Version history](version-history.md).

## Windows says "Windows protected your PC".

That is SmartScreen, because the installer is not signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. Read [Install Lilo](install.md).

## Where do I report a problem?

Read [Report a bug or a machine](bug-reports.md).

pages.body:
# Report a bug or a machine

Lilo is open source. Problems and machine reports go to the Lilo project on GitHub (github.com/Kadwood/lilo, **Issues**). There are two forms.

## Report a bug

Choose **Bug report** and fill in:

1. **What happened.** Say what you did, what you expected and what you got.
2. **Your system.** Mac, Windows or Linux, and the Lilo version. The version is in **Lilo Link**, **Settings**.
3. **A project file.** If you can, attach the .lilo file. It lets us see the design.
4. **Logs.** For a send problem, copy the text from **Lilo Link**, **Logs**.

A screenshot helps a lot.

## Report a machine

Choose **Machine report** to tell us how Lilo worked with your machine. We list machines as **tested** only after a real sew-out. Your report moves a machine from "should work" to "works". Fill in:

- The **brand and model**.
- Whether the **Wi-Fi scan** found it.
- Whether **Send** worked.
- Whether the design **sewed**.
- Any error **code** you saw. Read [Wi-Fi troubleshooting](send-troubleshooting.md).

## Before you report

- Check [Wi-Fi troubleshooting](send-troubleshooting.md) or [Fixing sew-out problems](sewout-troubleshooting.md).
- Update to the newest Lilo.
- Do not include private information. Lilo does not send anything automatically.
